extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, Chairs, Scientific Officers and committee members participating in the CIHR Project Grant competition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for conducting committee-based peer review of CIHR Project Grant applications, including assignment, review preparation, meeting conduct, scoring, and post-meeting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of review
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR's principles of review are: confidentiality, absence of conflict of interest, fairness, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles underpin all reviewer behaviour and decisions throughout assignment, review writing, committee discussion, and post-meeting actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must exercise rigorous scientific judgement, be fair and reasonable, and take into account, in a balanced way, the particular context of each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constructive review should point out strengths and weaknesses to help applicants improve future submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and authorship of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be written in the reviewer's own words and must not be directly copied from elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy comments from other reviewers, your own previous reviews, or use text generated by artificial intelligence tools; the use of AI-generated text constitutes a breach of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening assessment of research contributions and impacts (DORA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should look broadly beyond traditional indicators (e.g., h-index) when assessing contributions and impacts and focus on assessing quality and impact directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the context of the applicant, additional valuable research outputs, and non-traditional contributions rather than relying on simple bibliometric measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Progress — content and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary of Progress is a mandatory two-page document that contextualizes the application within the applicant's research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should outline activities, contributions and impacts supporting the current application, explain why requested funds are needed and how the budget is distinct from other funds, and may describe the impact of leave, career stage, pandemic, family responsibilities or other circumstances. It should be a narrative, not a detailed accounting (funding details are in the CV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions treated as new applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications, including resubmissions, must be treated as new applications and reviewed relative to other applications in the current competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an applicant indicates resubmission status, reviewers should not give special preferential treatment; consult Resubmissions webpage for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to previous reviews — visibility and optionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants resubmitting may include a Response to Previous Reviews attachment; this is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will see the Response to Previous Reviews only if the applicant has included the Previous Reviews attachment. The Response and Previous Reviews are independent of the resubmission question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant CV requirements and reviewer assessment of team expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic applicants must use CIHR Biosketch CV; non-academics and some others may use Applicant Profile CV (max three pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate CVs along with the Most Significant Contributions to assess the complement of expertise, experience and resources relative to the project's objectives, and assess productivity broadly while taking context into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of productivity and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are to assess productivity broadly by considering a range of contributions and impacts as well as contextual factors that may have affected progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual factors (career stage, leave, pandemic, responsibilities, etc.) should be taken into account when judging productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory appendices and other application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read all Other Application Materials provided; mandatory appendices include SGBA certificate and specific letters (pending appointment letter, employer letter for international paid researchers, Indigenous community support letters where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application includes non-eligible appendices or missing mandatory items, bring it to CIHR staff attention as soon as possible. Consult Task 8 of the Application Instructions for details on mandatory, optional, and no-longer-accepted attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for applicant-prepared attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicant-prepared attachments must use a minimum of 12 point, Times New Roman font in black type. Other fonts/sizes may be used only for text in tables, charts, figures, graphs and legends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text in non-standard fonts must be legible when viewed at 100%; if not legible at 100%, reviewers are not required to read or account for them in their assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of applications and expertise declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to three committee members based on alignment with declared expertise; reviewers must declare conflicts of interest and indicate expertise level (High, Medium, Low, or Not enough expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reviewer is not automatically conflicted by being at the same institution as the applicant if they do not know or work with the applicant. If, upon seeing full applications, a reviewer feels they lack appropriate expertise for an assigned application, they must contact CIHR immediately for reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer preparatory tasks in ResearchNet
rubrics_metrics.description: For each assigned application, reviewers must provide a summary of the project demonstrating understanding, list strengths and weaknesses based on adjudication criteria, provide initial ratings and initial budget recommendations prior to the meeting, and designate each application as top-ranked or bottom-ranked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial ratings must be to one decimal place and submitted five business days before the committee meeting; sex and gender-based analysis must be evaluated in the strengths and weaknesses and will factor into the overall initial score. Budget recommendations should be specific to item and amount and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission deadlines and revision window
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews (including overall quality assessment, top/bottom group designation, initial rating, and initial budget recommendations) must be uploaded to ResearchNet five business days before the committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once submitted, reviews cannot be modified prior to the meeting; reviewers may revise their reviews during or after the committee meeting and have five business days after the meeting to complete changes. Save work often as ResearchNet may time-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining criteria for removing applications from discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is streamlined (removed from discussion) if it meets three conditions: (1) the average reviewers' scores places it in the bottom 60% of all applications in the committee; (2) at least one reviewer placed it in their non-competitive (bottom) group; and (3) there is no objection from any committee member to streamline the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with fewer than three reviews cannot be streamlined. Streamlined applicants still receive written reviews from assigned reviewers but no detailed Scientific Officer notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion order and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: If not streamlined, discussion proceeds with assigned reviewers presenting: first reviewer gives synopsis and strengths/weaknesses (including sex/gender considerations), the other two reviewers follow addressing agreements/disagreements, assigned reviewer reads external referee reviews (if provided), Chair opens discussion to all committee members, Scientific Officer reads back SO notes capturing key discussion elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should use gender-neutral and inclusive language during presentations and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rating and Chair determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair seeks a consensus rating from the three assigned reviewers. If consensus cannot be reached, the Chair determines the consensus rating, usually by using the mean value of the assigned reviewers' ratings after discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers announce initial ratings to one decimal place and may revise them during discussion; the Chair's determination is applied when assigned reviewers cannot agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final committee voting and rating adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: All committee members not in conflict (excluding the Chair and Scientific Officers) are asked to vote to plus or minus 0.5 of the consensus rating for the final rating of each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process generates the final rating used in CIHR's post-meeting collection of ratings and funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget verification and recommendation specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to verify the requested budget and justification and may recommend that the budget remain as requested or recommend reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed budget cut must be justified and be specific about which item, by how much, and why. CIHR will seek recommendations from reviewers on budgets and terms requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-meeting collection, notices, and pending flags
rubrics_metrics.description: After the committee meeting, CIHR collects final ratings and recommendations on funding level and grant term from all committee members; applicants receive a Notice of Recommendation, copies of reviews and Scientific Officer notes, followed by a Notice of Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications flagged for special attention are withheld as 'pending' and applicants are notified if further information is required. If approved, Notices include allocated funds information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling non-eligible attachments and administrative issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application includes appendices that are not eligible or instructions appear not to have been followed, reviewers should bring this to the attention of CIHR staff as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative irregularities should be raised early to allow CIHR staff to address them prior to or during review processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gender-neutral and inclusive language
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is encouraged to use gender-neutral and gender-inclusive language when presenting reviews and engaging in discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of conduct expectations during committee meetings and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: External referee reviews handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If external reviews have been provided by external referees, one of the three assigned reviewers reads these reviews during the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers should integrate external referee comments into their presentation of strengths and weaknesses where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise reassessment after full application access
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible that after seeing the full application, a reviewer may decide they do not have appropriate expertise to review the assigned application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this occurs, the reviewer must contact CIHR immediately so the application can be re-assigned appropriately.
